# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

| Measure | Threshold or "record only" |
|---|---|
| Line coverage | record only |
| Branch coverage | record only |
| Mutation score | record only; a surviving mutant that a test should plausibly have caught is a finding |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

# Scope

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)

2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.

# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are derived in phase 1 as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).

# Architecture

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 0, 2, 4, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

## Components

Each component gets its own folder and README in `02_output/`. Versions come only from `tech-stack.md`; reference its ids, never repeat a version here.

```yaml
components:
  - name: backend
    type: api
    folder: 02_output/backend
    platform: java
    build: maven-wrapper
    bootstrap: Maven wrapper plus a hand-written pom.xml whose parent is org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent; root package si.konferenca.registration
    commands:          # ES-05; filled in phase 0 if left empty
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: []
    deploys_as: container image (eclipse-temurin base, non-root)
  - name: frontend
    type: web-app
    folder: 02_output/frontend
    platform: node
    build: vite
    bootstrap: hand-written package.json with the exact tech-stack.md versions and a committed package-lock.json (no project generator)
    commands:
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: [backend]
    deploys_as: container image (static files served by nginx)
```

The local stack (both components, PostgreSQL, mail catcher) is started with `02_output/docker-compose.yml`.

## Constraints

Checkable rules the code must respect (layering, allowed dependencies, patterns). Checked automatically in phase 6 where the stack allows (DoD-04).

| ID | Constraint |
|---|---|
| AR-01 | The frontend talks to the backend only through the REST API under `/api`. |
| AR-02 | The backend's internal architecture is not prescribed: the agent declares and justifies it in `docs/02_specification.md` and then writes ArchUnit rules that check exactly that declaration. |
| AR-03 | No package cycles in the backend (ArchUnit slice check). |
| AR-04 | Conference options change through configuration only, without code changes and without changing the fixed participant fields (BR-01). The mechanism is decided in phase 2. |
| AR-05 | A success response is sent only after both the database row and the JSON copy are written (BR-06, BR-07). |
| AR-06 | The database schema changes only through Flyway migrations (ES-08). |
| AR-07 | The frontend contains no secret; the reCAPTCHA site key is its only key and comes from configuration. |

## Interfaces

Every interface between components or with external systems is defined as a contract in `docs/02_contracts/` in phase 2.

| Interface | Between | Style (e.g. REST, gRPC, events, file, UI) |
|---|---|---|
| Registration form | participant and frontend | UI |
| Options, registration, export | frontend or organizer and backend | REST (OpenAPI) |
| Registration storage | backend and PostgreSQL | SQL (JPA) |
| JSON copy | backend and persistent volume | file (JSON schema) |
| Conference options | configuration and backend | file or configuration (schema defined in phase 2) |
| Emails | backend and SMTP server | SMTP |
| Anti-automation | frontend, backend and Google reCAPTCHA | JavaScript widget, HTTPS verify call |

## Thresholds

| Measure | Threshold or "record only" |
|---|---|
| Line coverage | record only |
| Branch coverage | record only |
| Mutation score | record only; a surviving mutant that a test should plausibly have caught is a finding |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |

---
name: write-acceptance-tests
description: Write and freeze the black-box acceptance tests from the acceptance criteria and contracts, before any production code exists (phase 3).
---

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phase 3 · Agent: read-only

- Reads: `docs/01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/phases.md`
- Writes: acceptance and end-to-end tests, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`
- Does not read: production source code

## Procedure

1. For every AC, write at least one test through the component's public interface that checks the observable outcome the AC states. For a rejection AC, also check that nothing changed.
2. Put the AC id in each test name.
3. Run the suite. Every test must fail because the behaviour is missing, not because of a build, configuration or harness error; a test that passes only on bootstrap code is listed in step 4. Fix the harness until that holds.
4. Record the run (pass/fail counts and a one-line reason per group of failures) in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`.
5. Self-check every assertion and helper before the freeze, because a defective frozen test costs a blocking decision: confirm that a correct implementation can make it pass, and that it cannot pass or fail for the wrong reason. Check what each helper returns and what each matcher compares (known cases: the PostgreSQL JDBC driver returns java.sql.Timestamp, not OffsetDateTime, for 	imestamptz unless the type is requested; AssertJ doesNotContain on a  yte[] tests single bytes, not a byte sequence, so compare the first bytes with Arrays.copyOf instead). A test must not contradict another assertion in the same test.
6. Format and lint the tests now; after freezing they cannot change.
7. Commit the tests story by story as you finish them. Then write the manifest (normalised line endings) and commit it alone as the freeze commit.

# Acceptance criteria

> Written in: phase 1 · Source: `project/01_requirements/*` · Agent: writes (frozen after phase 3)

Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. Open questions are answered by decision records D-05 … D-10 (pending review).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, D-08 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, D-06 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, D-05 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, D-06 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, D-05 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, D-07 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |
| US-002 | AC-002-01 … AC-002-07 |
| US-003 | AC-003-01 … AC-003-03 |
| US-004 | AC-004-01 … AC-004-04 |
| US-005 | AC-005-01 … AC-005-04 |
| US-006 | AC-006-01 … AC-006-03 |
| US-007 | AC-007-01, AC-007-02 |
| US-008 | AC-008-01 … AC-008-04 |

Total: 35 criteria. Open questions: OQ-01 → D-05, OQ-02 → D-06, OQ-03 → D-07, OQ-04 → D-08, OQ-05 → D-09, OQ-06 → D-10.

Requirements without their own criterion, covered in the specification and verified in phase 6: SR-03 rate and size limits, NFR-02 persistence across container recreation, NFR-04 health and readiness (runtime demonstration).

## D-05: OQ-01 option availability by registration type
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: OQ-01 unanswered in \`scope.md\`; US-002 speaks of "activities available to students".
- Options: 1. every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both), and the backend rejects an option not available to the type (default); 2. every active option is available to everyone.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1: configuration-only, rejects rather than silently accepts; with the default of both types it behaves like option 2)

## D-06: OQ-02 mandatory consents and wording
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: OQ-02 unanswered; BR-05 requires mandatory consents, never preselected.
- Options: 1. consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory); the shipped configuration has one mandatory consent \`privacy\`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." (default); 2. hard-code consents.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1); the wording must be confirmed by the product owner before production

## D-07: OQ-03 storage succeeds but an email fails
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: OQ-03 unanswered; scope priority 1: storage comes before any notification.
- Options: 1. the registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown); emails are sent only after the database row and JSON copy exist; a failure is logged with the registration id only (no personal data) so an operator can resend from the JSON copy (default); 2. roll back the registration when an email fails.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1; option 2 would lose registrations, contrary to priority 1)

## D-08: OQ-04 number of options per category
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: OQ-04 unanswered.
- Options: 1. no per-category limit; each option at most once per registration, duplicates rejected (default); 2. at most one option per category.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1; an invented limit could lock out legitimate users, a High severity example)

## D-09: OQ-05 second registration with the same email
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: OQ-05 unanswered.
- Options: 1. allowed; each registration is stored separately and organizers see both in the export (default); 2. reject a duplicate email.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review (option 1: never loses a registration, and a rejection would reveal to anyone whether an email is registered)

## D-10: OQ-06 retention of registrations and JSON copies
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1

input.content:
# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

## 1. System overview

Two components (`architecture.md`): `backend` (Spring Boot REST API, Java 21) and `frontend` (React single page built by Vite, served by nginx). Locally `02_output/docker-compose.yml` runs backend, frontend, PostgreSQL and Mailpit; in production an external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend container and forwards `/api` to the backend container.

The frontend calls only `/api/**` with relative URLs (AR-01). In the local stack the frontend's own nginx forwards `/api` to the backend, so the browser sees one origin and CORS is not needed; the Vite dev server proxies `/api` the same way.

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02 declaration)

Ports and adapters around a framework-light domain. Root package `si.konferenca.registration`.

| Package | Responsibility | May depend on (application packages) |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | Model (`RegistrationType`, `Registration`, `ConferenceOption`, `ConsentDefinition`, …), business rules (`RegistrationValidator`), use case (`RegistrationService`), ports (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `ConferenceCatalog`) | none |
| `api` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, request filters (rate and size limits, HTTPS-only organizer guard) | `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, implementation of `RegistrationStore` | `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | Raw JSON copy files, implementation of `JsonCopyStore` | `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | Participant and organizer emails, implementation of `RegistrationNotifier` | `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | reCAPTCHA verification (test mode and production), implementation of `CaptchaVerifier` | `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | Excel workbook generation | `domain` |
| `adapter.catalog` | Loads and validates the conference configuration file, implementation of `ConferenceCatalog` | `domain` |
| `config` | Spring wiring, typed properties, security configuration, startup safety checks | all of the above |

Justification: the domain holds every business rule (BR-01 … BR-08) and can be tested without Spring MVC, JPA or SMTP; each external system (PostgreSQL, file system, SMTP, Google, configuration file) sits behind one port so the order "store, then notify" (AR-05, D-07) is expressed once in `RegistrationService`. Dependencies point inwards only.

ArchUnit rules (DoD-04), in `src/test/java/.../architecture/ArchitectureTest.java` (phase 5):

1. `domain` depends on no other application package and on no `org.springframework.web..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `org.springframework.data..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.springframework.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..` class.
2. `api` depends only on `domain` among application packages.
3. Each `adapter.*` package depends only on `domain` among application packages (no adapter → adapter, no adapter → `api`, no adapter → `config`).
4. Only `config` may depend on `adapter.*` (besides the adapter itself).
5. No cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03).
6. Flyway is the only schema source: `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate` (AR-06, checked by configuration test).

## 3. Configuration (ES-01, AR-04)

Environment variables (Spring relaxed binding). "—" = no default; the application refuses to start without it.

| Setting | Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Environment name | `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `production`, `local` or `test`. Defaulting to `production` makes every production safety check apply unless an environment opts out. |
| Database URL, user, password | `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | — | compose supplies them; tests use Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection`. Password from `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. |
| SMTP host, port, TLS | `SPRING_MAIL_HOST`, `SPRING_MAIL_PORT`, `APP_MAIL_STARTTLS` | —, `25`, `true` | local: Mailpit, TLS off. Connection, read and write timeouts 5 s. |
| SMTP account | `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty | production only. |
| Sender address | `APP_MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | |
| Organizer recipients | `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | — | comma separated, each validated at startup. |
| Conference name | `APP_CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | shown in emails and on the page. |
| Conference configuration file | `APP_CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | classpath `conference-options.json` | production refuses the classpath default (`environments.md`: default allowed local/test only). |
| JSON copy directory | `APP_JSON_COPY_DIR` | `data/json-copies` | created at startup if missing; on a named volume in compose. |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | `APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | SR-02. |
| reCAPTCHA keys | `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | required unless test mode. |
| reCAPTCHA verify URL | `APP_RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | overridden only in tests (mock endpoint). |
| Organizer login | `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | — | password ≥ 16 characters, hashed with BCrypt at startup; the plain value is not kept. |
| Organizer HTTPS-only | `APP_ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | may be `false` only when `APP_ENVIRONMENT` is not `production`. |
| CORS allowed origin | `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty (CORS off) | allowed only when `APP_ENVIRONMENT=local`. |
| Rate limits | `APP_RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATION_PER_MINUTE`, `APP_RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE`, `APP_RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | `10`, `120`, `10` | per client address, fixed one-minute window. |
| Request-size limit | `APP_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16384` | request bodies on `/api/**`. |

Startup safety checks (`config.StartupSafetyChecks`), all fail the start with a message naming the setting (never its value): in `production`, test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys, HTTPS-only off, CORS origin set, or the classpath conference configuration (SR-02, environments.md); in every environment, empty organizer username/password, password shorter than 16 characters, empty or invalid organizer email list, invalid conference configuration (AC-003-03).

### Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, D-05, D-06)

A JSON file validated against `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json` at startup and held in memory; changing options means editing the file and restarting the backend. Participant fields are fixed in code (BR-01) and are not part of the file. Additional semantic checks: option and consent ids unique; at least one option category value from the enum; `availableTo` non-empty. Any violation stops the start (AC-003-03). The shipped file `src/main/resources/conference-options.json` contains sample options in every category and the consent `privacy` from D-06.

## 4. REST API (contract: `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Operation | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | Conference name, captcha settings (`mode` `test` or `recaptcha`, `siteKey`), consents, active options (AC-003-01, AC-003-02). Inactive options are never returned. |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited, reCAPTCHA | Validates, stores, writes the JSON copy, answers 201, then sends emails (sections 5–7). |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer (HTTP Basic), rate limited, HTTPS-only guard | Excel workbook of all registrations (section 8). |
| `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not under `/api` (not forwarded by the production proxy) | NFR-04, ES-09. Details hidden. |

Every other path answers 401/403/404 without internal detail. Errors use one body shape: `{"message": "...", "fieldErrors": [{"field": "...", "message": "..."}]}`. Status codes: 400 validation or rejected captcha, 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, 403 organizer credentials over plain HTTP (SR-06), 413 body too large, 415 wrong content type, 429 rate limit, 503 captcha verifier unreachable, 500 any other error (generic message, ES-07).

### Registration validation (domain, SB-01, BR-01 … BR-05)

Applied in this order; all field errors of one request are returned together.

1. Unknown JSON properties → 400 (`spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true`); `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
2. Every string is trimmed (BR-02); required fields of the type must be non-empty after trimming; fields of the other type must be absent or empty (fixed fields, BR-01 — field error "not allowed for this registration type").
3. Lengths: names ≤ 100, email ≤ 254, organization / study institution / study programme ≤ 200, student ID ≤ 50. Any Unicode letter is allowed (BR-03, NFR-01).
4. Email: `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` and parseable by `jakarta.mail.internet.InternetAddress(strict)`; this also excludes line breaks (SR-05).
5. Options: each id must exist, be active and be available to the type; duplicates are rejected (BR-04, SR-04, D-05, D-08). Field `optionIds`.
6. Consents: every mandatory consent id must be in `consentIds`; unknown ids are rejected. Field `consents.<id>` (BR-05).
7. Captcha: `captchaToken` must be present and verified (SR-01). Field `captchaToken`. Verification runs only when steps 1–6 passed, so invalid input costs no call to Google.

## 5. Storage (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

`RegistrationService.register` performs, in one database transaction: insert the registration with its options and consents (flushed), then write the JSON copy; the transaction commits only after the copy is written. If the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted. The 201 response is sent only after commit (AR-05).

Database (contract `02_contracts/database.md`, Flyway `V1__registration_schema.sql`): tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`; option name and category and the consent text are stored as they were at registration time, so later configuration changes do not alter stored registrations. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`, `open-in-view=false`. All queries via Spring Data / JPA parameters (SB-05).

JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`): one UTF-8 file `<registration-id>.json` in `APP_JSON_COPY_DIR`, written to a temporary file in the same directory and moved atomically. Content: the registration as accepted (trimmed values, options with name and category, consents with text and time); never the captcha token or any internal field (SR-07).

Registration ids are random UUIDs generated by the backend.

## 6. Participant email (US-006, SR-05, D-07)

Sent after commit on a background executor (so the response does not wait for SMTP), one plain-text UTF-8 message to the participant address (contract `02_contracts/email.md`). Subject contains only the configured conference name. User input appears only in the body; plain text means markup is never interpreted (SR-05); the recipient is the validated address. A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not affect the accepted registration (AC-006-03, D-07).

## 7. Organizer notification (US-007, SR-07)

After commit, one plain-text message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, listing the registration data, with the JSON copy file attached as `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored copy, AC-007-02). Same failure handling as section 6.

## 8. Excel export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

`GET /api/export` returns `registrations.xlsx` (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) generated with Apache POI. Sheet `Registrations`, header row, one row per registration ordered by registration time. Columns: Registration ID, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), Type, First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (option names, `; ` separated), Consents (`id at time`). All values written as string cells, so no cell is evaluated as a formula (SB-05).

Access (SB-02, SB-03, SR-06): Spring Security HTTP Basic, single in-memory organizer with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies). Before authentication a filter refuses (403, no body data) any `/api/export` request that is not secure, unless the client address is loopback or HTTPS-only is off. Tomcat's remote-IP handling (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`) trusts `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` only from internal proxy addresses (Tomcat default), so the production proxy's HTTPS is recognised and a client cannot fake it directly.

## 9. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05; contract `02_contracts/recaptcha.md`)

`CaptchaVerifier` has two implementations selected by `APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`:

- Test mode (test and local only): token `TEST-PASS` is accepted, any other token rejected; no network call.
- Production: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to the verify URL with a 5 s timeout; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. An answer with `success: false` → 400; no answer, non-200 or unparsable → 503. Tested against a mocked endpoint (an in-test HTTP server), including a rejected token (DoD-P05).

The frontend renders the Google widget only in `recaptcha` mode, with the site key from `/api/form-config` (AR-07); in `test` mode it shows a note and sends `TEST-PASS`.

## 10. Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)

`api.RequestLimitFilter` before Spring Security: per client address (after remote-IP resolution) and per endpoint group (form configuration, registration, export), a fixed one-minute window counter in memory with the configured limit; above it → 429 with `Retry-After`. Request bodies on `/api/**` above `APP_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` → 413 (checked by `Content-Length` and by counting the stream). Old windows are evicted. The export limit also limits failed logins (PA-04 evidence).

## 11. Security headers, CORS, errors (SB-07, SB-10, ES-07)

- Backend responses: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; HSTS on secure requests.
- Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`.
- CORS: none unless `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set (local only), then exactly that origin for `/api/**`, `GET`/`POST`.
- A global exception handler maps every exception to the error shape without stack traces or class names; `server.error.include-*=never`. Logs contain registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data or secrets.

## 12. Frontend (UI contract: `02_contracts/ui.md`)

One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`; the participant picks the type (radio), fills the fixed fields of that type, picks options (checkboxes grouped by category; for a student only options available to students), ticks consents (never preselected, BR-05), solves the captcha and submits. Client-side validation (required, email format, mandatory consents) runs before any request (AC-004-03, NFR-03); server field errors are shown next to their fields (AC-004-02); a server or network failure shows a general error (AC-004-04); success replaces the form with the confirmation (AC-004-01, BR-06). Text is rendered by React (escaped, SB-05). No secrets in the bundle (AR-07).

## 13. Deployment, health, privacy

- Images: backend `eclipse-temurin` JRE base, runs as a non-root user; frontend built in `node` and served by unprivileged nginx on port 8080 inside the container (SB-11). Health checks: backend `/actuator/health/readiness`, frontend `/`, PostgreSQL `pg_isready` (NFR-04).
- Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02).
- Local ports bound to `127.0.0.1` only: frontend 8081, backend 8080, Mailpit UI 8025.
- Production reverse proxy example `02_output/deploy/nginx-production.conf.example`: TLS, HTTP→HTTPS redirect, `/` → frontend, `/api/` → backend, `proxy_set_header Host` set to a fixed upstream name and `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr` (SR-08), `client_max_body_size 16k`.
- Personal data (SB-12, SB-13): exactly the fields in `security-requirements.md`; purpose as listed there; retention per D-10 (operator deletes ≤ 12 months after the conference). Consent explicit, never preselected (SB-14).

## Traceability

| AC / SR / SB / NFR / AR | Section |
|---|---|
| AC-001-01, AC-002-01 | 4, 5 |
| AC-001-02, AC-002-02, AC-001-03 | 4 (validation 2) |
| AC-001-04, AC-002-03 | 4 (validation 4) |

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `01_acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

## 1. System overview

Two components (`architecture.md`): `backend` (Spring Boot REST API, Java 21) and `frontend` (React single page built by Vite, served by nginx). Locally `02_output/docker-compose.yml` runs backend, frontend, PostgreSQL and Mailpit; in production an external nginx terminates TLS, serves `/` from the frontend container and forwards `/api` to the backend container.

The frontend calls only `/api/**` with relative URLs (AR-01). In the local stack the frontend's own nginx forwards `/api` to the backend, so the browser sees one origin and CORS is not needed; the Vite dev server proxies `/api` the same way.

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02 declaration)

Ports and adapters around a framework-light domain. Root package `si.konferenca.registration`.

| Package | Responsibility | May depend on (application packages) |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | Model (`RegistrationType`, `Registration`, `ConferenceOption`, `ConsentDefinition`, …), business rules (`RegistrationValidator`), use case (`RegistrationService`), ports (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `ConferenceCatalog`) | none |
| `api` | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, error mapping, request filters (rate and size limits, HTTPS-only organizer guard) | `domain` |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, implementation of `RegistrationStore` | `domain` |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | Raw JSON copy files, implementation of `JsonCopyStore` | `domain` |
| `adapter.mail` | Participant and organizer emails, implementation of `RegistrationNotifier` | `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | reCAPTCHA verification (test mode and production), implementation of `CaptchaVerifier` | `domain` |
| `adapter.export` | Excel workbook generation | `domain` |
| `adapter.catalog` | Loads and validates the conference configuration file, implementation of `ConferenceCatalog` | `domain` |
| `config` | Spring wiring, typed properties, security configuration, startup safety checks | all of the above |

Justification: the domain holds every business rule (BR-01 … BR-08) and can be tested without Spring MVC, JPA or SMTP; each external system (PostgreSQL, file system, SMTP, Google, configuration file) sits behind one port so the order "store, then notify" (AR-05, D-07) is expressed once in `RegistrationService`. Dependencies point inwards only.

ArchUnit rules (DoD-04), in `src/test/java/.../architecture/ArchitectureTest.java` (phase 5):

1. `domain` depends on no other application package and on no `org.springframework.web..`, `jakarta.persistence..`, `org.springframework.data..`, `jakarta.mail..`, `org.springframework.mail..`, `org.apache.poi..` class.
2. `api` depends only on `domain` among application packages.
3. Each `adapter.*` package depends only on `domain` among application packages (no adapter → adapter, no adapter → `api`, no adapter → `config`).
4. Only `config` may depend on `adapter.*` (besides the adapter itself).
5. No cycles between the slices `si.konferenca.registration.(*)..` (AR-03).
6. Flyway is the only schema source: `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate` (AR-06, checked by configuration test).

## 3. Configuration (ES-01, AR-04)

Environment variables (Spring relaxed binding). "—" = no default; the application refuses to start without it.

| Setting | Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Environment name | `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `production` | `production`, `local` or `test`. Defaulting to `production` makes every production safety check apply unless an environment opts out. |
| Database URL, user, password | `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD` | — | compose supplies them; tests use Testcontainers `@ServiceConnection`. Password from `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. |
| SMTP host, port, TLS | `SPRING_MAIL_HOST`, `SPRING_MAIL_PORT`, `APP_MAIL_STARTTLS` | —, `25`, `true` | local: Mailpit, TLS off. Connection, read and write timeouts 5 s. |
| SMTP account | `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | empty | production only. |
| Sender address | `APP_MAIL_FROM` | `registration@konferenca.si` | |
| Organizer recipients | `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | — | comma separated, each validated at startup. |
| Conference name | `APP_CONFERENCE_NAME` | `Conference` | shown in emails and on the page. |
| Conference configuration file | `APP_CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | classpath `conference-options.json` | production refuses the classpath default (`environments.md`: default allowed local/test only). |
| JSON copy directory | `APP_JSON_COPY_DIR` | `data/json-copies` | created at startup if missing; on a named volume in compose. |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | `APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `false` | SR-02. |
| reCAPTCHA keys | `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | empty | required unless test mode. |
| reCAPTCHA verify URL | `APP_RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | overridden only in tests (mock endpoint). |
| Organizer login | `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | — | password ≥ 16 characters, hashed with BCrypt at startup; the plain value is not kept. |
| Organizer HTTPS-only | `APP_ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `true` | may be `false` only when `APP_ENVIRONMENT` is not `production`. |
| CORS allowed origin | `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | empty (CORS off) | allowed only when `APP_ENVIRONMENT=local`. |
| Rate limits | `APP_RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATION_PER_MINUTE`, `APP_RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE`, `APP_RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | `10`, `120`, `10` | per client address, fixed one-minute window. |
| Request-size limit | `APP_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `16384` | request bodies on `/api/**`. |

Startup safety checks (`config.StartupSafetyChecks`), all fail the start with a message naming the setting (never its value): in `production`, test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys, HTTPS-only off, CORS origin set, or the classpath conference configuration (SR-02, environments.md); in every environment, empty organizer username/password, password shorter than 16 characters, empty or invalid organizer email list, invalid conference configuration (AC-003-03).

### Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, D-05, D-06)

A JSON file validated against `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json` at startup and held in memory; changing options means editing the file and restarting the backend. Participant fields are fixed in code (BR-01) and are not part of the file. Additional semantic checks: option and consent ids unique; at least one option category value from the enum; `availableTo` non-empty. Any violation stops the start (AC-003-03). The shipped file `src/main/resources/conference-options.json` contains sample options in every category and the consent `privacy` from D-06.

## 4. REST API (contract: `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Operation | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | Conference name, captcha settings (`mode` `test` or `recaptcha`, `siteKey`), consents, active options (AC-003-01, AC-003-02). Inactive options are never returned. |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited, reCAPTCHA | Validates, stores, writes the JSON copy, answers 201, then sends emails (sections 5–7). |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer (HTTP Basic), rate limited, HTTPS-only guard | Excel workbook of all registrations (section 8). |
| `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not under `/api` (not forwarded by the production proxy) | NFR-04, ES-09. Details hidden. |

Every other path answers 401/403/404 without internal detail. Errors use one body shape: `{"message": "...", "fieldErrors": [{"field": "...", "message": "..."}]}`. Status codes: 400 validation or rejected captcha, 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, 403 organizer credentials over plain HTTP (SR-06), 413 body too large, 415 wrong content type, 429 rate limit, 503 captcha verifier unreachable, 500 any other error (generic message, ES-07).

### Registration validation (domain, SB-01, BR-01 … BR-05)

Applied in this order; all field errors of one request are returned together.

1. Unknown JSON properties → 400 (`spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true`); `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
2. Every string is trimmed (BR-02); required fields of the type must be non-empty after trimming; fields of the other type must be absent or empty (fixed fields, BR-01 — field error "not allowed for this registration type").
3. Lengths: names ≤ 100, email ≤ 254, organization / study institution / study programme ≤ 200, student ID ≤ 50. Any Unicode letter is allowed (BR-03, NFR-01).
4. Email: `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` and parseable by `jakarta.mail.internet.InternetAddress(strict)`; this also excludes line breaks (SR-05).
5. Options: each id must exist, be active and be available to the type; duplicates are rejected (BR-04, SR-04, D-05, D-08). Field `optionIds`.
6. Consents: every mandatory consent id must be in `consentIds`; unknown ids are rejected. Field `consents.<id>` (BR-05).
7. Captcha: `captchaToken` must be present and verified (SR-01). Field `captchaToken`. Verification runs only when steps 1–6 passed, so invalid input costs no call to Google.

## 5. Storage (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

`RegistrationService.register` performs, in one database transaction: insert the registration with its options and consents (flushed), then write the JSON copy; the transaction commits only after the copy is written. If the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted. The 201 response is sent only after commit (AR-05).

Database (contract `02_contracts/database.md`, Flyway `V1__registration_schema.sql`): tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`; option name and category and the consent text are stored as they were at registration time, so later configuration changes do not alter stored registrations. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`, `open-in-view=false`. All queries via Spring Data / JPA parameters (SB-05).

JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`): one UTF-8 file `<registration-id>.json` in `APP_JSON_COPY_DIR`, written to a temporary file in the same directory and moved atomically. Content: the registration as accepted (trimmed values, options with name and category, consents with text and time); never the captcha token or any internal field (SR-07).

Registration ids are random UUIDs generated by the backend.

## 6. Participant email (US-006, SR-05, D-07)

Sent after commit on a background executor (so the response does not wait for SMTP), one plain-text UTF-8 message to the participant address (contract `02_contracts/email.md`). Subject contains only the configured conference name. User input appears only in the body; plain text means markup is never interpreted (SR-05); the recipient is the validated address. A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not affect the accepted registration (AC-006-03, D-07).

## 7. Organizer notification (US-007, SR-07)

After commit, one plain-text message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, listing the registration data, with the JSON copy file attached as `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored copy, AC-007-02). Same failure handling as section 6.

## 8. Excel export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

`GET /api/export` returns `registrations.xlsx` (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) generated with Apache POI. Sheet `Registrations`, header row, one row per registration ordered by registration time. Columns: Registration ID, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), Type, First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (option names, `; ` separated), Consents (`id at time`). All values written as string cells, so no cell is evaluated as a formula (SB-05).

Access (SB-02, SB-03, SR-06): Spring Security HTTP Basic, single in-memory organizer with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies). Before authentication a filter refuses (403, no body data) any `/api/export` request that is not secure, unless the client address is loopback or HTTPS-only is off. Tomcat's remote-IP handling (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`) trusts `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` only from internal proxy addresses (Tomcat default), so the production proxy's HTTPS is recognised and a client cannot fake it directly.

## 9. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05; contract `02_contracts/recaptcha.md`)

`CaptchaVerifier` has two implementations selected by `APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`:

- Test mode (test and local only): token `TEST-PASS` is accepted, any other token rejected; no network call.
- Production: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to the verify URL with a 5 s timeout; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. An answer with `success: false` → 400; no answer, non-200 or unparsable → 503. Tested against a mocked endpoint (an in-test HTTP server), including a rejected token (DoD-P05).

The frontend renders the Google widget only in `recaptcha` mode, with the site key from `/api/form-config` (AR-07); in `test` mode it shows a note and sends `TEST-PASS`.

## 10. Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)

`api.RequestLimitFilter` before Spring Security: per client address (after remote-IP resolution) and per endpoint group (form configuration, registration, export), a fixed one-minute window counter in memory with the configured limit; above it → 429 with `Retry-After`. Request bodies on `/api/**` above `APP_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` → 413 (checked by `Content-Length` and by counting the stream). Old windows are evicted. The export limit also limits failed logins (PA-04 evidence).

## 11. Security headers, CORS, errors (SB-07, SB-10, ES-07)

- Backend responses: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; HSTS on secure requests.
- Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`.
- CORS: none unless `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set (local only), then exactly that origin for `/api/**`, `GET`/`POST`.
- A global exception handler maps every exception to the error shape without stack traces or class names; `server.error.include-*=never`. Logs contain registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data or secrets.

## 12. Frontend (UI contract: `02_contracts/ui.md`)

One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`; the participant picks the type (radio), fills the fixed fields of that type, picks options (checkboxes grouped by category; for a student only options available to students), ticks consents (never preselected, BR-05), solves the captcha and submits. Client-side validation (required, email format, mandatory consents) runs before any request (AC-004-03, NFR-03); server field errors are shown next to their fields (AC-004-02); a server or network failure shows a general error (AC-004-04); success replaces the form with the confirmation (AC-004-01, BR-06). Text is rendered by React (escaped, SB-05). No secrets in the bundle (AR-07).

## 13. Deployment, health, privacy

- Images: backend `eclipse-temurin` JRE base, runs as a non-root user; frontend built in `node` and served by unprivileged nginx on port 8080 inside the container (SB-11). Health checks: backend `/actuator/health/readiness`, frontend `/`, PostgreSQL `pg_isready` (NFR-04).
- Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02).
- Local ports bound to `127.0.0.1` only: frontend 8081, backend 8080, Mailpit UI 8025.
- Production reverse proxy example `02_output/deploy/nginx-production.conf.example`: TLS, HTTP→HTTPS redirect, `/` → frontend, `/api/` → backend, `proxy_set_header Host` set to a fixed upstream name and `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr` (SR-08), `client_max_body_size 16k`.
- Personal data (SB-12, SB-13): exactly the fields in `security-requirements.md`; purpose as listed there; retention per D-10 (operator deletes ≤ 12 months after the conference). Consent explicit, never preselected (SB-14).

## Traceability

Startup safety checks (`config.StartupSafetyChecks`), all fail the start with a message naming the setting (never its value): in `production`, test mode on, empty reCAPTCHA keys, HTTPS-only off, CORS origin set, or the classpath conference configuration (SR-02, environments.md); in every environment, empty organizer username/password, password shorter than 16 characters, empty or invalid organizer email list, invalid conference configuration (AC-003-03).

### Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, D-05, D-06)

A JSON file validated against `02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json` at startup and held in memory; changing options means editing the file and restarting the backend. Participant fields are fixed in code (BR-01) and are not part of the file. Additional semantic checks: option and consent ids unique; at least one option category value from the enum; `availableTo` non-empty. Any violation stops the start (AC-003-03). The shipped file `src/main/resources/conference-options.json` contains sample options in every category and the consent `privacy` from D-06.

## 4. REST API (contract: `02_contracts/openapi.json`)

| Operation | Access | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/form-config` | public, rate limited | Conference name, captcha settings (`mode` `test` or `recaptcha`, `siteKey`), consents, active options (AC-003-01, AC-003-02). Inactive options are never returned. |
| `POST /api/registrations` | public, rate limited, size limited, reCAPTCHA | Validates, stores, writes the JSON copy, answers 201, then sends emails (sections 5–7). |
| `GET /api/export` | organizer (HTTP Basic), rate limited, HTTPS-only guard | Excel workbook of all registrations (section 8). |
| `GET /actuator/health`, `/actuator/health/liveness`, `/actuator/health/readiness` | public, not under `/api` (not forwarded by the production proxy) | NFR-04, ES-09. Details hidden. |

Every other path answers 401/403/404 without internal detail. Errors use one body shape: `{"message": "...", "fieldErrors": [{"field": "...", "message": "..."}]}`. Status codes: 400 validation or rejected captcha, 401 missing/wrong organizer credentials, 403 organizer credentials over plain HTTP (SR-06), 413 body too large, 415 wrong content type, 429 rate limit, 503 captcha verifier unreachable, 500 any other error (generic message, ES-07).

### Registration validation (domain, SB-01, BR-01 … BR-05)

Applied in this order; all field errors of one request are returned together.

1. Unknown JSON properties → 400 (`spring.jackson.deserialization.fail-on-unknown-properties=true`); `type` must be `EXTERNAL` or `STUDENT`.
2. Every string is trimmed (BR-02); required fields of the type must be non-empty after trimming; fields of the other type must be absent or empty (fixed fields, BR-01 — field error "not allowed for this registration type").
3. Lengths: names ≤ 100, email ≤ 254, organization / study institution / study programme ≤ 200, student ID ≤ 50. Any Unicode letter is allowed (BR-03, NFR-01).
4. Email: `^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` and parseable by `jakarta.mail.internet.InternetAddress(strict)`; this also excludes line breaks (SR-05).
5. Options: each id must exist, be active and be available to the type; duplicates are rejected (BR-04, SR-04, D-05, D-08). Field `optionIds`.
6. Consents: every mandatory consent id must be in `consentIds`; unknown ids are rejected. Field `consents.<id>` (BR-05).
7. Captcha: `captchaToken` must be present and verified (SR-01). Field `captchaToken`. Verification runs only when steps 1–6 passed, so invalid input costs no call to Google.

## 5. Storage (US-005, BR-07, AR-05, AR-06, ES-08)

`RegistrationService.register` performs, in one database transaction: insert the registration with its options and consents (flushed), then write the JSON copy; the transaction commits only after the copy is written. If the copy fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after the copy was written, the copy is deleted. The 201 response is sent only after commit (AR-05).

Database (contract `02_contracts/database.md`, Flyway `V1__registration_schema.sql`): tables `registration`, `registration_option`, `registration_consent`; option name and category and the consent text are stored as they were at registration time, so later configuration changes do not alter stored registrations. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`, `open-in-view=false`. All queries via Spring Data / JPA parameters (SB-05).

JSON copy (contract `02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json`): one UTF-8 file `<registration-id>.json` in `APP_JSON_COPY_DIR`, written to a temporary file in the same directory and moved atomically. Content: the registration as accepted (trimmed values, options with name and category, consents with text and time); never the captcha token or any internal field (SR-07).

Registration ids are random UUIDs generated by the backend.

## 6. Participant email (US-006, SR-05, D-07)

Sent after commit on a background executor (so the response does not wait for SMTP), one plain-text UTF-8 message to the participant address (contract `02_contracts/email.md`). Subject contains only the configured conference name. User input appears only in the body; plain text means markup is never interpreted (SR-05); the recipient is the validated address. A send failure is logged with the registration id only and does not affect the accepted registration (AC-006-03, D-07).

## 7. Organizer notification (US-007, SR-07)

After commit, one plain-text message to every address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, listing the registration data, with the JSON copy file attached as `registration-<id>.json` (`application/json`, the exact bytes of the stored copy, AC-007-02). Same failure handling as section 6.

## 8. Excel export (US-008, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)

`GET /api/export` returns `registrations.xlsx` (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) generated with Apache POI. Sheet `Registrations`, header row, one row per registration ordered by registration time. Columns: Registration ID, Registered at (UTC ISO-8601), Type, First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (option names, `; ` separated), Consents (`id at time`). All values written as string cells, so no cell is evaluated as a formula (SB-05).

Access (SB-02, SB-03, SR-06): Spring Security HTTP Basic, single in-memory organizer with the BCrypt hash of `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD`; stateless, no session, no CSRF token needed (no cookies). Before authentication a filter refuses (403, no body data) any `/api/export` request that is not secure, unless the client address is loopback or HTTPS-only is off. Tomcat's remote-IP handling (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`) trusts `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` only from internal proxy addresses (Tomcat default), so the production proxy's HTTPS is recognised and a client cannot fake it directly.

## 9. Anti-automation (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05; contract `02_contracts/recaptcha.md`)

`CaptchaVerifier` has two implementations selected by `APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE`:

- Test mode (test and local only): token `TEST-PASS` is accepted, any other token rejected; no network call.
- Production: `POST` form `secret`, `response`, `remoteip` to the verify URL with a 5 s timeout; accepted only if the JSON answer has `"success": true`. An answer with `success: false` → 400; no answer, non-200 or unparsable → 503. Tested against a mocked endpoint (an in-test HTTP server), including a rejected token (DoD-P05).

The frontend renders the Google widget only in `recaptcha` mode, with the site key from `/api/form-config` (AR-07); in `test` mode it shows a note and sends `TEST-PASS`.

## 10. Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)

`api.RequestLimitFilter` before Spring Security: per client address (after remote-IP resolution) and per endpoint group (form configuration, registration, export), a fixed one-minute window counter in memory with the configured limit; above it → 429 with `Retry-After`. Request bodies on `/api/**` above `APP_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` → 413 (checked by `Content-Length` and by counting the stream). Old windows are evicted. The export limit also limits failed logins (PA-04 evidence).

## 11. Security headers, CORS, errors (SB-07, SB-10, ES-07)

- Backend responses: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`; HSTS on secure requests.
- Frontend nginx: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`.
- CORS: none unless `APP_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set (local only), then exactly that origin for `/api/**`, `GET`/`POST`.
- A global exception handler maps every exception to the error shape without stack traces or class names; `server.error.include-*=never`. Logs contain registration ids, never names, emails or other personal data or secrets.

## 12. Frontend (UI contract: `02_contracts/ui.md`)

One page. On load it fetches `/api/form-config`; the participant picks the type (radio), fills the fixed fields of that type, picks options (checkboxes grouped by category; for a student only options available to students), ticks consents (never preselected, BR-05), solves the captcha and submits. Client-side validation (required, email format, mandatory consents) runs before any request (AC-004-03, NFR-03); server field errors are shown next to their fields (AC-004-02); a server or network failure shows a general error (AC-004-04); success replaces the form with the confirmation (AC-004-01, BR-06). Text is rendered by React (escaped, SB-05). No secrets in the bundle (AR-07).

## 13. Deployment, health, privacy

- Images: backend `eclipse-temurin` JRE base, runs as a non-root user; frontend built in `node` and served by unprivileged nginx on port 8080 inside the container (SB-11). Health checks: backend `/actuator/health/readiness`, frontend `/`, PostgreSQL `pg_isready` (NFR-04).
- Named volumes `pgdata` and `jsoncopies` keep data across container recreation (NFR-02).
- Local ports bound to `127.0.0.1` only: frontend 8081, backend 8080, Mailpit UI 8025.
- Production reverse proxy example `02_output/deploy/nginx-production.conf.example`: TLS, HTTP→HTTPS redirect, `/` → frontend, `/api/` → backend, `proxy_set_header Host` set to a fixed upstream name and `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr` (SR-08), `client_max_body_size 16k`.
- Personal data (SB-12, SB-13): exactly the fields in `security-requirements.md`; purpose as listed there; retention per D-10 (operator deletes ≤ 12 months after the conference). Consent explicit, never preselected (SB-14).

# Contract: anti-automation (frontend, backend, Google reCAPTCHA v2)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: specification section 9, SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05 · Agent: writes

## Frontend widget

- `GET /api/form-config` → `captcha.mode`, `captcha.siteKey`.
- `recaptcha` mode: load `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js?render=explicit` and render the v2 checkbox with `siteKey`; the token from the widget is sent as `captchaToken`. Submit stays possible only with a token (client check); the widget is reset after a rejected submission.
- `test` mode: no script is loaded; the page shows "Test mode: captcha disabled" and sends `captchaToken: "TEST-PASS"`.

## Backend verification (production code path)

Request: `POST <APP_RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL>` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, fields `secret=<RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY>`, `response=<captchaToken>`, `remoteip=<client address>`. Timeout 5 s.

Response handling:

| Verifier answer | Result |
|---|---|
| 200, JSON with `"success": true` | accepted |
| 200, JSON with `"success": false` (any `error-codes`) | rejected → API 400, field `captchaToken` |
| non-200, unparsable body, timeout, connection error | unavailable → API 503, nothing stored |

## Test mode (test and local only)

`APP_RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`: token `TEST-PASS` accepted, every other token rejected (400); no network call. Production (`APP_ENVIRONMENT=production`) refuses to start with test mode on or with an empty site or secret key (SR-02).
EOF

# Contract: registration form (participant ↔ frontend)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: specification section 12, US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, BR-05, BR-06 · Agent: writes

The acceptance and end-to-end tests find elements only by the roles, accessible names and texts below.

## Page

- Heading level 1: `Conference registration` followed by the conference name from `/api/form-config` (for example `Conference registration – Konferenca 2026`). While loading: text `Loading…`. If the configuration cannot be loaded: an element with role `alert` and text `The registration form is currently unavailable. Please try again later.`
- Radio group (role `radiogroup`, name `Registration type`) with radios `External participant` (checked by default) and `Student`.

## Fields (each an `<input>` with a visible `<label>`; accessible name = label)

| Field | Label | Shown for | Input type |
|---|---|---|---|
| firstName | `First name` | both | text |
| lastName | `Last name` | both | text |
| email | `Email` | both | email |
| organization | `Organization / institution` | external | text |
| studyInstitution | `Study institution` | student | text |
| studyProgramme | `Study programme` | student | text |
| studentId | `Student ID` | student | text |

Fields of the other type are not rendered. Values typed into the shared fields are kept when the type changes.

## Options

One `fieldset` (role `group`) per category that has at least one option available to the selected type, with legend `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (in this order). Each option is a checkbox whose accessible name is the option name. None is checked initially. Options not available to the selected type are not rendered.

## Consents

A `fieldset` with legend `Consents`; each consent is a checkbox whose accessible name is the consent text (mandatory ones end with ` *`... no: the text is the name; mandatory is signalled by `aria-required="true"`). Never checked initially (BR-05).

## Captcha

`recaptcha` mode: container with id `recaptcha` for the widget. `test` mode: text `Test mode: captcha disabled`.

## Submit

Button `Register`. While the request runs the button is disabled and named `Registering…`.

## Validation and errors (NFR-03)

- Client-side, on submit, before any request: empty required field → `This field is required.`; invalid email (`^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` after trimming) → `Enter a valid email address.`; unticked mandatory consent → `This consent is required.`. - Other failure (network, 5xx, 413, 429): role `alert` with text `Registration could not be completed. Please try again later.` and no confirmation (AC-004-04). 429 uses `Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.`

## Confirmation (BR-06, AC-004-01)

Shown only after a 201 response, replacing the form: heading level 2 `Registration received`, text `Thank you, <first name> <last name>. Your registration has been received.`, a list of the selected option names (or `No options selected.`), and `Registration ID: <id>`.
EOF

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: specification section 9, SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05 · Agent: writes

## Frontend widget

- `GET /api/form-config` → `captcha.mode`, `captcha.siteKey`.

Without a token the client shows `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` and sends nothing; the widget is reset after a rejected submission.

|---|---|

# Contract: registration form (participant ↔ frontend)

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: specification section 12, US-001, US-002, US-004, NFR-03, BR-05, BR-06 · Agent: writes

The acceptance and end-to-end tests find elements only by the roles, accessible names and texts below.

## Page

- Heading level 1: `Conference registration – <conference name>` (conference name from `/api/form-config`). While loading: text `Loading…`. If the configuration cannot be loaded: role `alert` with text `The registration form is currently unavailable. Please try again later.`
- Radio group (role `radiogroup`, name `Registration type`) with radios `External participant` (checked by default) and `Student`.

## Fields (each an `<input>` with a visible `<label>`; accessible name = label)

| Field | Label | Shown for | Input type |
|---|---|---|---|
| firstName | `First name` | both | text |
| lastName | `Last name` | both | text |
| email | `Email` | both | email |
| organization | `Organization / institution` | external | text |
| studyInstitution | `Study institution` | student | text |
| studyProgramme | `Study programme` | student | text |
| studentId | `Student ID` | student | text |

Fields of the other type are not rendered. Values typed into the shared fields are kept when the type changes. The form has `noValidate`, so only the rules below apply.

## Options

One `fieldset` (role `group`) per category that has at least one option available to the selected type, with legend `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities` (in this order). Each option is a checkbox whose accessible name is the option name. None is checked initially. Options not available to the selected type are not rendered; a checked option that becomes unavailable on a type change is unchecked.

## Consents

A `fieldset` with legend `Consents`; each consent is a checkbox whose accessible name is the consent text; mandatory consents have `aria-required="true"`. Never checked initially (BR-05).

## Captcha

See `recaptcha.md`: element with id `recaptcha` in `recaptcha` mode; text `Test mode: captcha disabled` in `test` mode.

## Submit

Button `Register`. While the request runs the button is disabled.

## Validation and errors (NFR-03)

- Client-side, on submit, before any request: empty required field (after trimming) → `This field is required.`; invalid email (`^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$` after trimming) → `Enter a valid email address.`; unticked mandatory consent → `This consent is required.`. No request is sent while any client error exists (AC-004-03).
- A field error is rendered as text next to its field; the input gets `aria-invalid="true"` and its accessible description (`aria-describedby`) is the error message. Server field errors (`fieldErrors[].field`) map to the same fields; `consents.<id>` to that consent's checkbox; `optionIds` to a text under the options; `captchaToken` to a text under the captcha; any other field to the general error.
- Server rejection (400): messages next to their fields; entered values stay (AC-004-02).
- Other failure (network, 5xx, 413): role `alert` with text `Registration could not be completed. Please try again later.`, no confirmation (AC-004-04). 429: role `alert` with text `Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.`

## Confirmation (BR-06, AC-004-01)

Shown only after a 201 response, replacing the form: heading level 2 `Registration received`, text `Thank you, <first name> <last name>. Your registration has been received.`, a list of the selected option names (or `No options selected.`), and `Registration ID: <id>`.
